tasks.subject: Fix a mistake: corrections.toml for claims, a fix page on every build, nav and footer links (#373) (#374)

prompts.spec:
# Fix a mistake: reader-facing corrections page, claim corrections file, nav link on every page

The site is generated, not edited. Readers who spot a wrong claim, a topic on the wrong page or a bad kind have no obvious way to fix it, and the only mechanism that exists today is `topics.toml`. A wrong claim cannot be fixed at all.

## Deliverables

1. **`infovore/wiki/corrections.toml`**, a claim-level correction file. An entry matches a claim by `exchange` id plus the exact `statement` as printed under Sources, and either `drop = true` or `replace = "new wording"`. `load_claims` applies it after scrubbing; dropped claims count under `excluded` as `corrected`, replaced claims keep their id. Because `_prose` already keeps only sentences whose cited claims are on the page, a drop removes the dependent prose at the next build with no rewrite. A replace shows at once under Sources and the prose catches up on the next article run. `stats` and `build` print `corrections unmatched: N` when an entry matches nothing, so typos are visible.
2. **A `fix.md` / `fix.html` page** written by every build: what the site is, why hand edits do not work, the two files a PR can change, with an example entry of each, and the issue tracker for anything else.
3. **Nav link `Fix a mistake` on every page** plus a footer line `Spotted a mistake? Fix it.`
4. **README section** pointing at the same two files.

Naming of the site (wiki vs digest) is a separate decision and not changed here.

tasks.subject: wiki: --background C lists established claims under Background and keeps them out of sections and the writer (#353) (#356)

prompts.spec:
# Net-new check: rank and label claims by novelty against a reference corpus before they reach the wiki

Eric, 2026-10-11: "Are we testing if the claims are net-new before writing them to the wiki? If not we should. Obviously IRIX runs on an Octane. That's old and well established info."

We are not. Today a claim reaches a page if it passes the verdict gate and its topic has 3 claims; corroboration only orders groups within a section. "The Octane runs IRIX (+3 similar; 4 speakers)" is the first line of Octane / With IRIX because it is the most corroborated statement there, and it is also the least informative.

Design, programmatic throughout (RULE #313: no LLM judgement over the corpus):

1. Reference corpus. Fetch the Wikipedia article (English, REST summary plus the plain-text extract) for every page topic that resolves to an exact title, cache it in a `reference_texts` table keyed by topic and fetched_at. Split into sentences. Expect a few hundred topics to resolve; that covers the hardware, OS and vendor pages where "well established" lives. Later: SGI techpubs and the IRIX Network wiki if their terms allow.
2. Novelty score. Embed claim statements and reference sentences with bge-small (already in `--extra embed`). For each claim, novelty = 1 minus the max cosine to any reference sentence for its topics. Also an intra-corpus generic score: the fraction of a claim's content tokens that are topic names or the top 50 corpus-wide tokens; "The Octane runs IRIX" scores 1.0, a war story about a specific PSU fault scores near 0.
3. Storage. `claim_novelty(claim_id, reference_max_cosine, reference_topic, generic_share, computed_at)`, filled by `infovore claims novelty --run R --tag-run T [--write]`, idempotent, read-only on everything else.
4. Use. `wiki build|stats --novelty-floor F` drops claims whose reference cosine is above 1 minus F (established elsewhere) from list sections and demotes them to the end of the page as "Background" with the Wikipedia link; group order within a section becomes (corroboration, novelty) so a corroborated novel claim leads. Writer units get only the novel leads.
5. Controls before anyone trusts it: the novelty distribution for claims on topics with a reference versus topics without; a hand-free sanity check by printing the 20 least novel and 20 most novel claims per sampled topic; and the share of claims on the Octane page above the floor.

Out of scope: judging truth (that is the claim check and #268), and anything that calls a model per claim.

tasks.subject: wiki: fold symbol, script, plural and generic-noun tag variants onto one topic (#352) (#354)

prompts.spec:
# Topic merge: fold symbol, script, plural and generic-suffix variants of one tag onto one page (refs #142)

Measured on tag run 1 (74,131 raw tags, 65,978 canonical keys after `canon.canonical`, 9,551 keys with 3+ claims). Four variant classes survive the current canonicalisation, which only casefolds, strips vendor prefixes, spaces, hyphens and dots:

| class | keys folded | claim-tags moved | examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| symbols and NFKC (®, ™, *, quotes, `()`, `$`, superscripts) | 131 | 185 | `bootp()` to bootp, Indigo² to Indigo2, $ORIGIN to Origin, *BSD to BSD |
| non-ASCII script around an existing key | 20 | 35 | O2机器 to O2, Fuel工作站 to Fuel, Numalink™ to NUMAlink |
| plural with the singular present | up to 3,326 | up to 13,621 | SGIs, Indys, O2s, Octanes, PSUs, power supplies, capacitors |
| generic noun suffix or "the" prefix | up to 1,220 | up to 2,401 | IRIX systems, O2 systems, Unix workstations, Alpha machines |

The last two need guards or they merge wrongly: Windows to window, XFS to xf, VMS to VM, Challenge S to Challenge, emacs to eMac, DOSBox to DOS, Xbox to X, Visual Workstation to visual. Guards that hold on the measured list: plural detection on the most common raw spelling (final lowercase `s`, not after a space, not `ss`), the suffix must be a separate word, and the target key must carry at least a quarter of the variant's claim count (so a 287-claim Windows never folds into a 6-claim window).

Plan:
- `canonical()` applies NFKC and strips ®™©*, quotes, `()` and a leading `$` (count-independent, so it stays a pure function).
- `merge_map(spellings)` in canon.py returns variant key to target key for script stripping, plurals and generic suffixes, with the guards above, computed once per build from the tag counts.
- `load_claims` maps each tag through canonical then merge_map; display names come from the merged spelling counts.
- `wiki stats` reports how many keys and claim-tags the merge folded.

Out of scope: translation of fully non-Latin tags (14 keys, 18 claim-tags), semantic merges (RS/6k vs RS/6000), and an authority file of canonical hardware names (#142).

tasks.subject: wiki build: one filename per topic, so colliding slugs no longer overwrite pages (#349) (#351)

prompts.spec:
# wiki build: page slugs collide and the later topic overwrites the page; non-ASCII topics slug to an empty filename

On the full build from tag run 1 (5,695 pages) \`slug()\` in \`infovore/wiki/topics.py\` lowercases and replaces every non \`[a-z0-9]\` run with \`-\`, and \`build_site\` keys files by it. 12 slugs are shared by 25 topics, and the last topic written wins:

- \`o2\`: O2 (one of the largest topics) and O2机器 (4 claims). o2.md is the 4-claim page.
- \`c\`: C, C#, C++. \`g\`: g, g++. \`hfs\`: HFS, HFS+. \`prboom\`: PrBoom, PrBoom+. \`gtk\`: GTK, gtk+.
- \`origin\`: $ORIGIN, Origin. \`path\`: $PATH, PATH. \`bootp\`: bootp, bootp(). \`indigo\`: Indigo, Indigo². \`intel-sc450nx\` with and without ®. \`radeon-driver\` with and without asterisks.

The topic 电源供应 slugs to the empty string, so its page is \`.md\` and See-also links point at \`(.md)\`.

Fix: \`build_site\` assigns one filename per topic: the topic with the most claims (then name order) keeps the plain slug, later colliders get \`-2\`, \`-3\`; an empty slug falls back to \`topic-<8 hex of sha1(name)>\`. Index and See-also links use the same mapping, so no link targets a missing or overwritten page.

The tagger emitting Chinese, ® and bracketed variants of one thing is a separate topic-merge problem (#142).

tasks.subject: wiki write --resume continues the latest matching article run instead of starting a new one (#348) (#350)

prompts.spec:
# wiki write --resume skips sections from earlier runs, so the resumed run lacks them and build --article-run shows claim lists

Seen on the first full write (SoHoT job 0078, article run 8, 2026-10-11): 6,569 sections written, none failed, yet \`wiki build --article-run 8\` renders every part-1 section of IRIX, Indigo2, Indy, O2 and Octane as a claim list. Those 146 sections were written in the 5-topic trial (run 7). \`written_sections\` in \`infovore/db/wiki_articles.py\` joins every run with the same model id, prompt hash and tag run, so \`--resume\` skipped them, while \`create_article_run\` still opened a new run. A logical write is therefore spread over several run ids, and the build reads one.

Run 8 has Octane sections \`General#2\`..\`General#37\` and \`With O2#2\`..\`#7\` but no \`General\`, \`With O2\`, \`With IRIX\`, ... (run 7 keys: 146, in run 8: 0).

Fix: \`--resume\` continues the latest run with the same model id, prompt hash and tag run, and skips only that run's sections. A new run is created only without \`--resume\` or when no run matches. \`claims extract --resume\` keeps its own semantics.

Then a resume job (~146 sections, about 7 minutes on Ornith-35B) fills run 8, queued on SoHoT behind the running code adopt job.

tasks.subject: claims controls: shuffled citations, overlap floor, matched lexicon recall, writer drops by verdict (#340) (#345)

prompts.spec:
# Negative controls for the claim check and the wiki gates

From the 2026-10-10 review. Every metric so far was computed on a target produced by the system under test and with no control.

Build `infovore claims controls` (read-only, CPU):
1. Shuffle citations within each exchange and recompute the deterministic check overlap; report the supported rate on shuffled pairs. If it stays near the real rate, the checker is lax and its verdicts mean little.
2. Pair each claim with a random claim from the same channel and month; its overlap with the wrong messages is the floor for `support.FLOOR`.
3. From article run 0078 (tonight): sentence drop rate in `keep_supported` by the verdict of the claims the sentence cites (supported / uncheckable / unsupported_fact / low_overlap). This is the free randomized read on #337.
4. Lexicon recall against a length- and position-matched sample of uncited messages, replacing the raw recall in #334.

Output: one table per control, JSON with `--json`. Author-cluster bootstrap for every interval (rows cluster by author and by exchange).

tasks.subject: wiki: Unsorted page for untagged claims, section parts instead of a group cap, loss accounting (#339) (#344)

prompts.spec:
# Wiki structural losses: orphan claims, MAX_GROUPS cut, min_claims 10

Audit 2026-10-10 (runs 13/14, tag run 1): after tech_only, 95,228 claims; `min_claims 10` leaves 61,411 on any page; 3,481 kept claims have no topic and appear nowhere; `MAX_GROUPS=40` sorts groups by size and cuts the smallest, dropping 35.4k of 52.6k groups, all singletons, which are the long-tail facts the archive exists to preserve.

Fix:
- Orphan claims (no topic) land on a Misc page keyed by lexicon term or speaker-free entity; never silently lost.
- Replace the MAX_GROUPS cut with batching: a section with more than 40 groups becomes several writer calls, all groups reach the writer.
- Default `min_claims` to 3 for write (GPU is free; cost is time).
- `wiki build` prints the loss accounting at every gate: in, out, dropped, reason.

tasks.subject: wiki: corroboration per claim group, embedding grouping, ordered by distinct speakers (#338) (#343)

prompts.spec:
# Corroboration score per claim cluster: distinct speakers and exchanges, embedding clustering

From the 2026-10-10 review. The only programmatic value signal every reviewer converged on: how many independent people, in how many separate conversations, said the same thing. Tag run 1 has 74,131 topics, 80% single-speaker; the signal exists and nothing uses it.

Build:
- Cluster claims within a topic by bge-small embedding similarity (reuse `triage/embed_stage`), not token Jaccard 0.5 (`wiki/groups.py`), which undercounts paraphrases. Keep Jaccard as a fallback when the embed extra is absent.
- Per cluster: distinct speakers, distinct exchanges, date span, and the verdict mix (#337).
- Expose it in `load_claims`/`group_claims`: clusters ordered by corroboration; singletons flagged as single-source rather than cut (#339).
- `wiki build` prints the corroboration distribution; pages show "N people, M conversations, first/last seen" per sentence group.

Metric (no labels): share of published sentences resting on clusters with 2+ speakers, before and after. Contradiction audit: sample 200 clusters and count merges of contradictory predicates (negation markers), as a check that embedding clustering does not merge "crashed" with "crashed after the patch".

This is the first step of #142 and the reframe recorded in the KB (corroboration-ranked, dated, source-linked index; prose only for corroborated clusters).

PR #248 strict relevant threshold (0.9876) decided only 24 relevant; residue grew 3,711 -> 19,619 of 115,513. Loosen: lowest threshold with CV precision >= 0.90 (--relevant-precision), irrelevant threshold rule (recall >= 0.95) unchanged. Print both thresholds with CV precision/recall/n; record in recipe_json.

# run loop: chunk + relevance cascade for new messages, no extraction; status on cascade outcomes

New messages stop at ingest. Run path should chunk (v2, incremental) then cascade --write new current exchanges, with no LLM stage; extraction becomes explicit-only. status should report current/archived/irrelevant/set aside/residue/last cascade/human labels/excluded channels.

Per channel: labelled, relevant, irrelevant, % irrelevant, total exchanges, excluded flag. Latest human_exchange label (bad_grouping excluded), reusing triage/human.training_labels. Sort by % irrelevant desc then labelled desc; --min-labels N (default 1); excluded channels marked, not hidden.

tasks.subject: Skip fragments: judge queues need 3 text messages; cascade no_text stage (#217) (#220)

prompts.spec:
# Skip fragment exchanges: judge queues need >=3 text messages; cascade sets text-less aside

54% of exchanges have 1-2 messages; 2,327 singletons are attachment-only. likely-irrelevant serves them first and they teach nothing. Dynamic judge queues (likely-irrelevant, uncertain, c1) serve only exchanges with >=3 non-empty text messages; cascade gets a no_text stage after denylist, excluded from accuracy. trainable_labels unchanged.
